# Normalizer points in groups generated by convex root subsets

This internal supporting module works over a field, for a connected reductive
group and a chosen maximal split torus. For a convex subset of its full
relative root set, membership of a rational torus-normalizing point in the
associated root-subset group is equivalent to membership of its Weyl class
in the reflection-generated Weyl subgroup of the symmetric roots.

`ConvexRootNormalizerWeylStatement` packages this equivalence over every
field, connected reductive group, maximal split torus, convex subset of
its full relative root set, and morphism satisfying `IsRootSubsetGroup`.
`convexRootNormalizerWeyl` proves the proposition. No reduced-root or
positive-rank hypothesis is imposed.

The proof chooses an integral cocharacter nonnegative on the subset and
vanishing among ambient roots exactly on its symmetric part. Minimality of
the root-subset group places it in the dynamic parabolic of this cocharacter:
positive root groups lie in the dynamic unipotent group, zero root groups
lie in the dynamic centralizer, and the entire torus centralizer also lies
there. A torus-normalizing parabolic point centralizes the cocharacter and
hence fixes it. The cocharacter stabilizer theorem identifies its Weyl class.

Conversely, a Weyl class in that subgroup fixes the cocharacter. Conjugation
on points shows that every normalizer representative centralizes it. The
root-generation theorem for rational points of the dynamic centralizer puts
the representative in the root-subset group, because it contains the
whole-torus centralizer and all zero-root groups.

For two individually convex subsets, the convex Weyl-group intersection
formula therefore proves equality on rational torus-normalizing points of
their two root-subset groups and the group of their common roots. Their
intersection is convex, using the intersection of the two defining cones.
No field extension or general reduced-point intersection is asserted here;
the chosen torus is assumed maximal split over the field in use.

The provenance is an internal derivation from the adapted integral
cocharacter, the dynamic parabolic normalizer-point theorem, the actual
cocharacter Weyl stabilizer, rational-point generation of the dynamic
centralizer, and the convex Weyl intersection formula. This module is a
supporting result for the group intersection statement
`ConvexRootSubsetGroupIntersectionStatement`, which is proved in
`Rational.ConvexRootSubsetGroupIntersectionProof`; it does not assert the
exact reduced-root group-scheme intersection statement.
